obs: St. Regis Paper Co. v. United States
“Ours is the duty to avoid a construction that would suppress otherwise competent evidence unless the statute, strictly construed, requires such a result.”
"A statute granting a privilege is to be strictly construed so as \"to avoid a construction that would suppress otherwise competent evidence.\""
"We have often recognized that statutes establishing evidentiary privileges must be construed narrowly because privileges impede the search for the truth."
